rv.q: It deserves more drama, emotion and political complexity on the ground.
The text stands confidently on its own, supported by the cast's performances rather than interesting staging and directorial conception.

The real takeaway is that a London theatre can, and does, dare to stage a new play about an important lesson from the past celebrating bold, risky international cooperation at a time when such courage has never been more required.

Perhaps the start of something very exciting – an interesting, insightful voice, brought together well with a standout design team and exciting cast - but just not necessarily told by the most important voice in the room.

cn.t: Mixed reviews greet this timely piece about international cooperation, with critics praising strong performances and design but finding the drama lacking in emotional depth and political complexity.
